authority_rule: This file is the sole authoritative project-management decision source. Other docs/data may describe implementation details but must not override requirements, priorities, decisions, conflicts, active gate, or quality status recorded here.
product_north_star: Let the player live the Peter Jackson film story as a playable adventure rather than inventing a replacement main story.
Make the world feel alive, beautiful, explorable and responsive while preserving story chronology and low-spec performance.
Preserve every meaningful user request and decision so chat loss or developer changes never erase project intent.
Prefer player enjoyment, clarity, stable traversal, save continuity and reliable performance over uncontrolled feature quantity.
operating_rules: Global project-management changes go through the single Governor and a validation branch/PR; workers must not create competing authority files.
One governor, one decision authority. No secondary file may independently redefine requirement status, priority, conflict resolution, active gate, or region acceptance.
Every meaningful user request receives a stable requirement ID here before or with implementation.
New requests never silently delete older requests; contradictions become explicit conflicts/decisions here.
The film story spine, build/save/story integrity, target-device performance and required traversal cannot be silently traded away.

Before changing or adding any FILM_CORE beat, verify the exact scene order, participating characters and outcome against the supplied film/script source; do not rely on memory when the source can be checked.
A feature is never called accepted from compile/static evidence alone.

If a previously passed critical gate fails, quarantine the affected acceptance/merge path, repair the smallest failing layer, and rerun the exact failed gate while unrelated safe production work continues.
Human pacing and visual review are mandatory for enjoyment/acceptance; CI cannot infer fun.
Developer-owned automation should reproduce and verify defects before asking the owner to spend play time on technical regression checks; never relabel machine checks as visual or pacing approval.

Validation harness semantics are first-class: repeated log copies must not inflate defect counts, save tests must prove disk roundtrip, and every failing debt gate must print concrete asset/package identities.
After W00 machine repair closure, do not delay W01 for invented repair work. Only concrete regression evidence may reopen architectural/root repair.
Final W00 automation must prove packaged runtime data and packaged executable startup before W01 opens.

Do not repeat an expensive UE4 build/cook/package gate merely because an immediate metadata parent was cancelled; reuse the nearest still-valid green proof only across an explicitly safe governance/docs-only ancestry, and fail closed if any runtime/asset/config/packaging path intervenes.

Local tracked launch controllers must never update themselves in place. Any helper that performs git pull while running must execute from an immutable temporary copy and preserve the explicit develop lane.

The programmer handoff must remain branch-simple: develop is canonical development/integration, main is stable/release, and temporary implementation branches self-clean after merge once meaningful content is integrated.
Temporary branches must merge meaningful completed work into develop immediately, then delete the branch ref; only active work or unresolved unique-content salvage may remain outside develop.

Parallel source/PDF/warehouse/asset-preparation lanes may advance without repeating engine gates for administrative-only changes; promotion into runtime remains serialized and technical safety/performance/runtime-data gates stay fail-closed.

Permanent branch closeout invariant: every completed temporary branch is exact-head validated, merged into develop immediately, and its remote ref is deleted after merge so develop never lags completed work. Only an active PR head or a branch with verified unique unsalvaged commits may remain temporarily.

requirements.intent: Consolidate startup grounding, transactional chapter streaming, committed-world/living-world coordination, V10 regional life, automated QA, and visual-performance guardrails into one ordered integration path before further large feature expansion.
implementation_refs: Chapter asset preload is now two-phase: preloaded assets are not promoted to resident until the destination world build and grounding transaction succeeds.
ChapterWorldRouter publishes a committed world revision only after supported builder creation, grounded player placement, and asset-bank commit.
Failed swaps restore the previous builder where possible and fail closed with player movement held.
LivingWorldDirector combines V10 chapter density/roles with committed-world revision synchronization and does not apply destination life/weather before visible-world commit.
V10 regional NPC roles/dialogue data and living-NPC intelligence plans are integrated into the comprehensive branch.
Player persistence now uses the same ChapterWorldRouter committed chapter/route/episode boundary used by living-world synchronization.
Saved transforms are grounded only after committed-world identity matches the restored save.
Failed-swap rollback snapshots now include player health/stamina/resolve/supplies and RestoreCommittedWorldFromSnapshot reapplies player-life state before releasing world hold.
Unreal Build workflow now attempts a guarded read/execute-only ACL repair for NETWORK SERVICE over UE4 Engine Content before running the unchanged engine-content verification gate.

A second ambientCG warehouse batch now targets non-Shire trilogy regions (Caradhras, Moria, Rohan, Gondor, Osgiliath/Ithilien, Mordor, Isengard, Bree/battlefields, Pelennor support and Shelob-lair support materials).
ChapterWorldRouter now publishes committed chapter/route/episode/revision into UShireNPCContextSubsystem on normal commit and rollback.
NPC regional mood/profile availability follows committed world identity; new bounded dialogue/film-context selection is suppressed while logical quest state and visible committed world disagree.
Character rig async handoff now releases completed FStreamableHandle ownership after player/NPC components take UObject references, preventing GameInstance-lifetime handle pinning.
All non-engine runtime LoadObject paths found in the audit were removed; chapter/world/enemy production meshes and audio now use resident-only soft resolution with async ownership/fallback contracts.
Shared grounding now handles bounded collision seams and capsule clearance; chapter-specific spawn pads are prohibited.
Character rig requests preflight package existence before async load, preserving modular fallback without missing-package engine errors.
missing_work: Preserve affected current-head transition/fault/persistence regression coverage; do not reopen historical integration solely because old missing-work wording remains.
Reconcile remaining V10 and ambient placement/pooling work against current source before adding density.
Target-device multi-chapter asset residency, GC and hitch measurements.
Human traversal/pacing/visual acceptance remains open beyond recorded P1C01 grounding evidence.
acceptance_criteria: No destination living-world state is applied before its geometry is committed.
No destination asset bank becomes resident before successful destination build and grounding.
Rapid/stale async transitions cannot publish the wrong visible world.
A failed swap does not publish a new world revision and fails closed rather than dropping the player.
P1C01 startup grounding regression remains required for runtime acceptance.
Exact-head machine gates and defect-specific PIE evidence remain distinct.
Persistence snapshots and restored transforms agree with the same committed world revision they describe.
Rollback never leaves logical quest state pointing at a different world from the visible restored builder.

requirements.title: Embodied third-person action-adventure camera is the default gameplay perspective
requirements.origin: Owner explicitly rejected top-down/RTS-style control and defined the goal as feeling physically present inside Middle-earth while directly controlling the character.
requirements.intent: Use a GTA/Red-Dead-like third-person embodied camera as the default exploration/combat/interaction perspective: camera behind or slightly over the player character, close enough to read the world and character but far enough for traversal/combat awareness. Do not use top-down, isometric or commander-style gameplay as the normal control mode.
implementation_refs: Current camera foundation already uses third-person follow/lag and character-scale offsets.
Temporary authored cinematic framing may override the gameplay camera only for bounded story presentation and must return safely to embodied control.
missing_work: Tune follow distance, shoulder/height offsets, FOV, camera collision and interior behavior per character scale.

acceptance_criteria: Normal movement directly controls the active character from a third-person behind/over-shoulder view.
The player never needs an RTS/top-down command view to explore or progress.

Camera collision prevents persistent wall/geometry clipping.
Interior/exterior transitions remain comfortable and do not break interaction targeting.
Cinematic camera moments return to the same embodied gameplay state without corrupting movement/save/route state.
requirements.notes: Primary goal is presence in the world: walk through, approach, touch/interact, fight and observe from the controlled character's physical position rather than directing units from above.

Warehouse staging has a dedicated concurrency group.
Exact-head checkout remains bounded/retried.
Provider staging, receipt reuse and inventory audit remain unchanged.

requirements.title: Use GitHub Pro capabilities without weakening project governance or low-spec production discipline
requirements.origin: Owner upgraded the personal GitHub account and explicitly requested that every materially useful GitHub Pro benefit be identified, used where appropriate, and recorded in the Project Governor.
requirements.intent: Exploit GitHub Pro for stronger private-repository controls, additional hosted CI reserve, development tooling and support while keeping the UE4.27 Windows build lane self-hosted, avoiding duplicate authorities, and preventing paid-feature usage from creating cost or workflow regressions.
implementation_refs: Personal GitHub account 4youbabee-tech owns the private fellowship-personal-game repository.

Owner-provided billing evidence shows a USD 4 charge from GITHUB, INC.; USD 4/month matches GitHub's published GitHub Pro monthly price. The connected GitHub tool does not expose the Billing 'Current plan' field, so the plan label itself remains UI-confirmation pending.
GitHub Pro published allowance: 3,000 GitHub-hosted Actions minutes/month for private repositories; self-hosted runner execution remains free and does not consume that allowance.
GitHub Pro published allowance: 180 Codespaces core-hours/month and 20 GB-month Codespaces storage for personal accounts.
GitHub Pro published allowance: 2 GB GitHub Packages storage and 10 GB/month Packages data transfer; current GitHub Actions artifact storage allowance is 1 GB.

GitHub Pro enables advanced private-repository controls including protected branches, required/multiple pull-request reviewers, code owners, auto-linked references, private-repository Pages/Wikis availability, and repository insights graphs.
GitHub Pro includes GitHub Support via email.
GitHub Pro does not include Copilot Pro and does not increase the published Git LFS 10 GB storage / 10 GB bandwidth allowance versus personal Free.
missing_work: Owner/UI confirmation of Settings > Billing and licensing > Current plan = GitHub Pro, because the connected GitHub API surface available to this project does not expose the current-plan field.

Enable protected-branch rules for develop and main after the current runtime train is safely integrated: block force-push/deletion and require appropriate CI status checks without requiring a second human reviewer while the project has a single maintainer.
Set billing budgets/alerts so optional hosted Actions, Codespaces and Packages cannot create accidental overage.
Add CODEOWNERS enforcement only when a second trusted maintainer/reviewer exists; do not create a self-review deadlock.
Use Codespaces only for lightweight repository work (JSON/docs/Python/static review), not UE4.27 Windows compilation or warehouse payload work.
Use Packages only for small versioned developer tooling/build metadata when it clearly replaces ad-hoc distribution; do not upload the multi-GB asset warehouse into the 2 GB Packages allowance.
acceptance_criteria: develop and main receive non-destructive branch protection appropriate to the single-maintainer workflow.
UE4.27 C++ build/import/runtime/package validation remains on the supervised self-hosted Windows runner unless a separately proven better lane exists.
GitHub-hosted Actions quota is treated as a reserve for isolated lightweight jobs, not as justification to move expensive Unreal work off the proven runner.
Codespaces/Packages usage is opt-in, budgeted and limited to workloads that materially benefit the project.
Pages/Wiki do not become a second project authority; ProjectGovernor remains the sole management authority and private/copyright-sensitive project material is not published accidentally.
No Pro feature may weaken exact-head validation, asset provenance, async loading, pooling, low-spec performance gates or canon controls.

hard_invariants.description: Meaningful user requirements and decisions must be persisted in repository data; chat history is never the sole source of truth.
Peter Jackson film continuity remains the primary story spine unless the user explicitly records a product-direction override.
A change must not knowingly introduce build failure, crash, save corruption, story deadlock or route-state loss.
Intended playable routes and required story anchors must not be accepted while blocked, trapping the player, or unreachable.
Features must remain compatible with the target laptop profile: Windows DX11, 720p, Low/Medium, 30 FPS floor target, 8 GB RAM, roughly 2 GB VRAM-class GPU.
Static/compile success must never be presented as PIE, device, performance, pacing or visual acceptance.

A runtime defect is never called fixed from source inspection or static validation alone. Identify the root cause, add a regression signal where feasible, pass exact-head machine gates, then require defect-specific PIE/device observation before closure.

The player must not receive gravity in chapter coordinates until the destination world is committed and blocking ground is confirmed. Startup and chapter audits fail closed when grounding cannot be proven.
Heavy production asset growth must follow soft/asynchronous chapter or region ownership; residual synchronous loading is debt to reduce, not a pattern to expand.
High-count non-story decorative detail uses HISM/ISM plus bounded culling where practical; do not multiply independent actors/ticks for foliage or repeated micro-detail.
Per-frame Tick is reserved for bounded time-sensitive behavior. Heavy loading, JSON/file I/O, or unbounded actor/world scans may not be introduced into Tick.
Baked, stationary, CSM and distance-field lighting/shadow choices are measured per scene/profile on the target laptop; no technique is globally declared cheaper without evidence.

Warehouse acquisition/cataloguing must not wait for UE runtime/PIE/device gates. Assets may be DISCOVERED/CANDIDATE/STAGED in bulk, but no file may be promoted to READY_FOR_IMPORT without intake validation (integrity, format, scale/unit, topology/UV/skeleton/texture sanity as applicable, provenance/metadata, and malware/archive hygiene). INTEGRATED and ACCEPTED states still require the relevant UE4.27 build/import/runtime/visual/audio/device evidence.

Expensive Unreal/package evidence is reused only across an explicit safe ancestry. Cancelled metadata parents do not force a recook when a nearby green ancestor remains valid, but any runtime/asset/config/streaming/packaging/unclassified delta breaks inheritance and requires the appropriate fresh lane.

develop is the sole canonical development/programmer-handoff branch and main is stable/release. Temporary branches are short-lived and removed after merge; stale diverged branches are never bulk-merged as a substitute for selective salvage.

conflict_rules: A new request never silently deletes or rewrites an older requirement.
If two active requirements conflict, the conflict must be explicitly recorded and resolved before either can be treated as fully accepted.
Hard invariants cannot be silently overridden by implementation convenience.
A user may explicitly change product direction; that override must be recorded as a decision and linked to affected requirements.
When no explicit user override exists, prefer preserving story/progress integrity and target-device playability over visual scope or feature quantity.
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request without destabilizing already validated behavior.

decisions.title: Film story anchors versus player exploration freedom
decisions.resolution: Major film chronology/outcomes remain fixed; exploration, side routes, optional conversations and living-world activity belong primarily between required story anchors.
decisions.rationale: Preserves the user's goal of living the film while allowing meaningful adventure and discovery.

decisions.title: Living-world richness versus target-laptop performance
decisions.resolution: Use rich near-player simulation and cheaper distance-adaptive/offscreen simulation; do not require always-on expensive AI for ambient life.
decisions.rationale: The world should feel alive without sacrificing the low-spec device target.

decisions.title: Source reorganization versus current functional validation gate
decisions.resolution: Define and guard the target Public/Private source architecture now, but perform the physical move as a dedicated maintenance pass after the current F9/F8/chapter/device functional gate is healthy.
decisions.rationale: Preserves organization without mixing a large path/include refactor into unresolved gameplay validation.

decisions.title: Begin a bounded visible character-production pass before the full functional hard gate is manually closed
decisions.resolution: Proceed with a small reversible Frodo/Gandalf visual-motion pass now because the user explicitly wants the game to start feeling playable. Do not change story/save architecture or add a large new subsystem; require static and UE4.27.2 build validation, then return to PIE/device gate evidence.
decisions.rationale: This satisfies the user's explicit current direction while limiting regression risk and preserving the existing hard-gate discipline.

decisions.title: Expand visible character production from player avatars to the full Part I core cast
decisions.resolution: Populate each Part I chapter with its required named cast and regional inhabitants now, while keeping expensive simulation near-player only and preserving film chronology. Use distinct proxies where dedicated production assets do not yet exist, and track those proxies as unfinished rather than pretending the cast is visually complete.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wants the world to start feeling inhabited and playable now; chapter-appropriate cast presence gives immediate experiential value without waiting for every final character asset.

decisions.title: Build first in larger batches, then perform a dedicated integration/playtest repair pass
decisions.resolution: Continue substantial character/world/runtime construction now while requiring Pre-Unreal and real UE4.27.2 compile/import gates for each merged batch. Defer detailed PIE, device, pacing and visual acceptance into a later dedicated integration/playtest/repair pass instead of stopping after every small visible feature.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wants to see a much more complete game when returning to the laptop and prefers building a larger playable body of work before manual testing.

decisions.title: Freeze after CP54 for real current-head PIE/device verification
decisions.resolution: Stop new checkpoints/content expansion after CP54. Verify the exact develop head in UE4.27 PIE chapter-by-chapter, beginning with Shire; repair blocking failures immediately; log non-blocking ideas only. Defer formal rights-holder outreach and resume material/world enrichment only after the baseline audit is complete.
decisions.rationale: Compile, import and headless startup are green, but the repository itself still records current-head traversal, performance, pacing and visual gates as untested for most chapters. Continuing to stack content would increase regression risk.

decisions.title: Lift the post-CP54 verification freeze and resume construction
decisions.resolution: Treat the post-CP54 verification pass as human-completed on the current validated develop baseline and resume large, guarded game-construction batches. Preserve Pre-Unreal and real UE4.27 build/import regression gates and continue to distinguish implementation from later visual/performance acceptance.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly confirmed that the planned verification/check/fix pass was completed and instructed the project to resume game construction and expansion.

decisions.title: Use the film chronology as the hard spine and expand playable life between anchors
decisions.resolution: For Part I, preserve Peter Jackson film chronology/outcomes as the non-negotiable main route. Expand Shire friendship, party life, companion banter, regional social texture, exploration and environmental storytelling in the spaces between those anchors. Prefer Extended Edition enrichment when compatible, but write original game dialogue and keep optional activity non-blocking.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly wants to feel present inside the film moment-to-moment while also having room to play, explore and enjoy the world.

decisions.title: Living NPC architecture is offline-only, local-first and bounded
decisions.resolution: Implement NPC identity, memory, schedules, goals, needs, emotions, relationships and knowledge limits entirely in local deterministic project systems. If a language model is later added, it must run locally/on-device and remain optional behind strict context/performance guards. Remote/cloud LLM, STT and TTS calls are not part of the shipped gameplay architecture.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly clarified that the game is offline. This also avoids API keys, internet dependency, recurring service cost, cloud outages and uncontrolled latency while protecting the 8 GB / ~2 GB VRAM target.

decisions.title: Shipped game AI must work with the internet disconnected
decisions.resolution: Treat offline execution as a hard product constraint. NPC intelligence, memory, relationships, schedules, goals, emotions, dialogue selection and any shipped speech/AI layer must not depend on remote services. Cloud APIs may be used only as developer-side tooling outside the shipped runtime, never as a gameplay dependency.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly stated that the game is offline and that the intelligent-NPC system must be offline at its foundation.

decisions.title: All Part I characters participate in the living-NPC layer
decisions.resolution: Treat living intelligence as a world-wide character rule, not a one-NPC demo. Named story characters receive rich biography, memory, relationships and knowledge envelopes; secondary named characters receive lighter persistent context; ambient populations use cheap archetype intelligence. All tiers remain offline and react to chapter mood, danger, weather and local context.
decisions.rationale: The project owner explicitly wants conversations with any character to feel like that character understands who they are, what has happened, and whether the surrounding world is peaceful, suspicious, grieving or at war.

decisions.title: PR #53 is the single CP56 mega-integration continuation path
decisions.resolution: Continue CP56/Work changes on PR #53 only. Keep develop unchanged until the current PR #53 head passes required validation.
decisions.rationale: One active integration branch prevents conflicting versions while we repair against one Actions result.

decisions.title: Adopt an exact-SHA automated quality gate without overstating proof
decisions.resolution: Extend the existing automation-first path instead of replacing it. Before merge, the exact candidate SHA should accumulate required evidence for Pre-Unreal/static checks, UE4.27 compile/import, startup/headless runtime, P1C01-P1C08 chapter audits, warning debt, story/route and save/load roundtrips, offline NPC behavior, text/localization integrity, plus target-device performance and memory evidence as those tests are implemented. Keep the established 720p Low-Medium 30 FPS floor target. Validate story consistency against project authorities (Governor, Story Canon Bible and FilmExperiencePlan). Produce machine-readable exact-SHA status plus a human-readable report. Introduce Unreal Automation Framework, Gauntlet and Unreal Insights incrementally where useful; do not discard proven Python/runtime checks or let test infrastructure replace game production.
decisions.rationale: The owner reviewed a programmer proposal for comprehensive automated quality checking and accepted the useful direction with project-specific corrections: exact evidence rather than absolute zero-bug claims, the existing 30 FPS target rather than an invented 60 FPS target, and project canon as the story authority.

decisions.title: Screenplays ground context, not verbatim runtime dialogue
decisions.resolution: Treat the supplied Fellowship and Two Towers screenplay PDFs as primary scene/dialogue-context references. Store derived chronology, mood, safe topics and future-knowledge blocks. Runtime dialogue stays original and bounded; the shipped game never needs the PDFs. Part I contexts are active now and Part II contexts are reference seeds until its runtime production begins.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants conversation to feel naturally embedded in the film world and broader than fixed scripted exchanges without requiring exact wording.

decisions.title: Use shader-compile time for non-blocking static/content expansion without bypassing the merge gate
decisions.resolution: While the target machine is busy compiling shaders or otherwise unavailable for UE rebuilds, continue work that can be statically reviewed: data contracts, dialogue coverage, exploration envelopes, source hygiene and validators. Keep the same PR #53 integration path and still require the final exact head to pass full UE4.27 validation before develop merge.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly asked not to sit idle while Unreal compiles shaders, but also wants broken gates repaired before integration.

decisions.title: Adopt Journey Discovery rewards instead of generic exploration XP
decisions.resolution: Use a first-time Journey Discovery system inspired by the satisfaction of discovery rewards in exploration RPGs, but fit it to this project's tone: brief discovery toast, Journey Insight, Chronicle/map/knowledge/companion unlocks and regional completion bonuses. Do not use raw combat-stat inflation, canon-changing rewards or story skips.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants the project to function as a complete exploration game as well as a playable film-spine experience.

decisions.title: Side content is off-camera film-context gap-fill, never an alternate story
decisions.resolution: Keep all mandatory story events and outcomes on the Peter Jackson film spine. Optional exploration may add original side games and moments only when they plausibly fit the same story window, location, available characters, knowledge state and emotional/danger context. Treat them as off-camera moments that could have happened between film scenes. They may reward exploration and deepen relationships/world knowledge, but cannot invent a competing major plot or alter canon.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants a complete game, not a film-only corridor, while explicitly rejecting deviation from the film's main story.

decisions.title: Raise the world visual bar above the earlier plain reference examples
decisions.resolution: Do not treat the previously shown external game screenshots as the final visual target. Aim for a more beautiful, cinematic and memorable Middle-earth presentation with strong vistas, layered terrain, richer materials/vegetation, water, atmosphere, lighting and chapter-specific visual identity. Achieve the higher beauty bar selectively and efficiently so the established 720p Low-Medium / 30 FPS target is not silently abandoned.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly rejected the earlier reference-image quality as not beautiful enough and wants a substantially more attractive world.

decisions.title: The Ring quest is the central state line; all other routes serve or surround it
decisions.resolution: Treat the One Ring as the persistent strategic/emotional axis. Frodo is the Part I bearer after Bilbo's transfer; parallel routes cannot become replacement Ring routes. The Part I split hands forward the Frodo/Sam Ring journey.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly reaffirmed the Ring as the axis of the series/game.

decisions.title: Use a dual-source character pipeline with provenance instead of waiting for one perfect external model
decisions.resolution: For each character, prefer a usable permitted external/project-owned base when available; otherwise build the character from legally usable/custom parts. External free/personal-use assets still require source and terms to be recorded before integration.
decisions.rationale: Owner wants immediate production and has multiple free/personal-use sources available, with custom 3D character creation as fallback.

decisions.title: Owner cinematic forest reference defines the higher environment beauty direction
decisions.resolution: Target the reference's dense naturalism, layered depth, strong light shafts, ground detail and embedded characters as the beauty direction, while using selective hero detail and optimization to preserve the 720p Low-Medium / 30 FPS floor.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly chose the supplied image as a better visual model than prior examples.

decisions.title: Treat the project as a modern narrative game wrapped around immutable film anchors
decisions.resolution: Mandatory Peter Jackson film anchors remain fixed. Between anchors, the game may add original plausible side missions, world events, exploration, companion activities, environmental puzzles, lightweight character-life systems and utility/content progression. These systems may deepen play but may not skip, reorder or alter film outcomes.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly asked to research what modern games contain and adopt fitting game systems throughout the project while keeping the film itself intact.

decisions.title: Film scenario is the non-negotiable story authority from beginning to end
decisions.resolution: For every mandatory story beat, scene order, character presence and outcome must follow the Peter Jackson film continuity. When screenplay/film source material is available, it must be checked before implementation; memory or invented connective logic may not override it. Original game content is permitted only in unused gaps around fixed anchors and must close or yield when the next canonical scene begins.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly reaffirmed that adherence to the film scenario from beginning to end is the highest story requirement and corrected any tendency to drift.

decisions.title: Do not make Frodo the default viewpoint when the film gives another character the action
decisions.resolution: Use Gandalf, Aragorn, Arwen, Boromir, Legolas, Gimli, Merry, Pippin, Sam and later-film characters as playable viewpoints when the film naturally centers the relevant action on them. Frodo remains the Ring-quest center, not the only playable character. Small original missions may expand verified gaps but may not displace fixed film scenes or outcomes.
decisions.rationale: Owner explicitly wants to exploit the trilogy's many non-Frodo mission opportunities and expand them slightly as game content.

decisions.title: Use four continuity classes plus explicit source-verification status
decisions.resolution: Classify side content as FILM_CORE, FILM_EXPANDED, FILM_INTERSTITIAL or BOOK_CHRONICLE. Track source verification separately. Book Chronicles never silently alter the main film timeline, and Part III stays FUTURE_SOURCE_CHECK until exact source verification is recorded.
decisions.rationale: The programmer proposal is valuable but a three-label system alone cannot distinguish original gap-fill from book-only alternate continuity or verified from unverified material.

decisions.title: Execute the project through one dependency-ordered master roadmap
decisions.resolution: All accepted unfinished work must be assigned to Data/MasterExecutionRoadmap.json. The roadmap is subordinate to ProjectGovernor and cannot override canon, evidence or requirement status. Large implementation continues in bundles: exact-head stability, Part I story/gameplay completeness, production characters/world, living-world/presentation polish, acceptance/performance, then source-verified Part II and Part III.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly asked to consolidate the large request set and begin large-scale work immediately without forgotten workstreams.

decisions.title: Adopt a layered Unreal automated QA immune system without replacing runtime/device/human proof
decisions.resolution: Use layered validation: static/pre-Unreal guards, UE Automation Framework tests, existing end-to-end runtime smoke/state/chapter audits, then target-device performance/soak and owner PIE/visual/pacing confirmation. Prefer deterministic authored probes and evidence-based thresholds over random tests or arbitrary global limits.
decisions.rationale: The external proposal is high-value, but several literal thresholds and test methods would create false confidence or false failures on this project's generated worlds and low-spec target.

decisions.title: Use measured hybrid visual-performance architecture instead of one-size-fits-all UE4 optimization recipes
decisions.resolution: Keep current async chapter banks and HISM/culling foundations. Prefer soft references, instancing, role-appropriate LODs, shared material-instance families and event/timer-driven logic. Use baked/static lighting, Distance Field Shadows, Cull Distance Volumes or World Composition only where the authored world topology and target-device measurements justify them.
decisions.rationale: The programmer proposal contains strong industry practices, but runtime-generated chapter geometry and the ~2 GB VRAM target make blanket lighting/world-streaming prescriptions unsafe.

decisions.title: Consolidate recent approved work into one comprehensive integration train
decisions.resolution: Use integration/comprehensive-foundation-v1 as the ordered convergence branch. Integrate startup grounding -> QA foundation -> performance guardrails -> V10 living-world content -> transactional transition coordination, validate exact head, then merge to develop. Do not independently merge overlapping #62/#63/#64/#65/#66 while the train is active.
decisions.rationale: Multiple individually useful branches now overlap the same runtime and governance surfaces. A single ordered integration train reduces regression risk and stops the project from spending more time on parallel repair branches than on coherent construction.

decisions.title: Adopt warehouse-first trilogy production in parallel with the P1C01 vertical slice
decisions.resolution: Maintain a comprehensive F1-F3 asset warehouse continuously instead of deferring final characters/world/audio to the end. Preproduction, sourcing and asset-bank construction may proceed across the trilogy in parallel, while runtime feature/chapter integration remains subject to the active foundation and exact-head gates. P1C01 Shire is the first fully assembled natural-looking benchmark used to prove the pipeline before mass application.
decisions.rationale: The project accumulated strong backend/governance coverage faster than visible production content. Warehouse-first production prevents recurring surprise gaps and turns asset acquisition/authoring into a persistent production lane rather than an ad hoc late task.

decisions.title: Separate warehouse intake validation from runtime acceptance
decisions.resolution: Run asset-warehouse filling continuously and independently from runner availability. Discovery, download/staging and catalogue enrichment do not wait for compile/PIE/device tests. Use a lightweight intake gate before READY_FOR_IMPORT; reserve UE4 import/build, PIE, performance and human visual/audio acceptance for assets that are actually integrated into a production slice.
decisions.rationale: Blocking warehouse fill on runtime gates wastes parallelizable production time; skipping all intake checks, however, converts the warehouse into an untrusted dump. The correct large-team pattern is staged asset ingestion with escalating proof requirements.

decisions.title: Parallelize world foundations beyond the Shire
decisions.resolution: Keep P1C01 as the first full production benchmark, but build reusable world foundations and warehouse stock in parallel for all major trilogy regions. This includes regional architecture, terrain/materials, vegetation/ecology, props, population/faction families, audio, lighting, VFX and traversal/collision contracts. Runtime Part II/III chapter implementation remains gated.

decisions.title: Third-person embodied perspective is the permanent gameplay default
decisions.resolution: Keep Shire Journey as a direct-control third-person action-adventure experience, broadly comparable in camera relationship to GTA V / Red Dead style play: behind or slightly over the active character with contextual camera tuning. Do not turn normal gameplay into top-down, isometric, RTS or squad-command control. Allow bounded cinematic camera shots only when they return cleanly to the player's embodied perspective.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants the game's central feeling to be inhabiting and touching Middle-earth, not observing it from above.

decisions.title: Reuse proven CI evidence without repeating expensive work
decisions.resolution: Use three validation cost classes: safe governance/docs/offline metadata inherits valid nearby green proof without UE execution; ordinary runtime/C++/Data/SourceAssets uses core build/import/Automation/runtime/warning validation without cook/package; Config/Build.cs/Target.cs/streaming/package/cook/release changes use the full package lane. If the immediate parent was cancelled, governance-only ancestry may search backward for the nearest green first-parent proof only when every intervening path is explicitly safe. Validation-policy-only classifier/Pre-Unreal edits may inherit a green parent without engine repetition.
decisions.rationale: Two days of W00 stabilization showed that repeating already-proven build/cook/package work wastes time and increases runner exposure without increasing confidence when only metadata changed. Evidence reuse must remain fail-closed and path-bounded so speed never weakens correctness.

decisions.title: Separate private-offline asset intake from distributable framework clearance
decisions.resolution: For the owner's private offline Shire Journey experience, uncertain or non-commercially-cleared art/audio may be classified and used only in an explicitly isolated PRIVATE_OFFLINE_ONLY lane without blocking local experimentation solely on commercial-license uncertainty. Such assets must remain tagged, replaceable and excluded from every distributable/commercial Framework package. The distributable Framework lane remains strict: only assets with clear redistribution/commercial entitlement may ship. Provider-access restrictions remain independent and binding: do not bypass authentication, paywalls, DRM, anti-bot controls or prohibited scraping.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants maximum private-production speed while preserving a clean framework that may later be sold. Classification/isolation is safer than deleting provenance or globally disabling license/access guards.

decisions.title: Global playable-film doctrine for the entire game world and full story
decisions.resolution: This doctrine is GLOBAL across the entire Shire Journey game, from the opening of the story through the final ending, across every chapter, region, character arc, settlement, dungeon, battlefield, travel segment and world-state transition. Shire/P1C01 is only the first implementation benchmark, not the scope of the rule. The player must feel physically present inside the film-continuity world rather than watching a chain of cutscenes or playing an unrelated open world. Canon-defining story beats and locked outcomes remain immutable. Between those beats, every chapter and region must expose interactive safe windows for embodied third-person exploration, optional conversations, world/household interaction, side activities, NPC life, fauna, environmental storytelling and local choice whenever chronology permits. Control may enter bounded cinematic/set-piece moments when required, then return cleanly to the player. Optional actions may change flavor, local relationships, discovery, pacing or minor world state, but must not invalidate the film's causal spine or locked chapter outcome. World/NPC/prop/audio state must transition coherently before and after each canon beat so the player feels the consequences in the playable world.
decisions.example_contract: F1-01/Bag End remains only the first benchmark example of the global rule. The same pattern must be applied chapter-by-chapter across the full game world: identify locked canon beats, surround them with playable safe windows, preserve chronology/outcomes, and return control into a world state that reflects what just happened.
acceptance_criteria: The doctrine applies to every chapter and every major playable region from the beginning of the story through the final ending; Shire/P1C01 is not an exception or the sole target.
Every major chapter identifies its locked canon beats and the playable safe windows around them.
Every major region identifies the world-life, exploration, interaction and environmental systems needed to make the player feel present inside that part of the story.
No required chapter is implemented as cutscene-only when an interactive safe window can preserve canon.
No free-roam/side activity can alter an immutable film outcome or create a contradictory chronology.
After a canon beat, NPC/world/prop/audio state reflects the new story state when the player regains control.
Dialogue added inside safe windows is original project-authored text and does not copy Tolkien or film dialogue verbatim.
Cinematic control transitions are bounded and return to the embodied third-person player cleanly.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly clarified that this is not a Shire/P1C01-specific design idea. It is a whole-game doctrine covering the complete world and full narrative: the player should inhabit and interact with the film continuity everywhere, while recognized story outcomes still unfold correctly.

decisions.title: Adopt the 225-source Master External Resource Bible as the global production sourcing map
decisions.resolution: The 68-page SHIRE_JOURNEY_MASTER_EXTERNAL_RESOURCE_BIBLE_V1_2026-09-25, containing 225 classified sources, is adopted as a global production-sourcing authority for the entire game. It does not override story/canon bibles. Its role is to diversify and prioritize sources for environment materials, vegetation, characters, rigging, animation, VFX, audio, music, UI/fonts, Arabic localization, terrain/GIS, scanning, AI-assisted creation and production tooling. Sourcing proceeds category-first using A then B then C priority, with provider-access restrictions preserved. The project converts the Bible into structured registry entries and category-specific acquisition waves rather than browsing randomly or copying all sources wholesale.
implementation_contract: Data/MasterExternalResourceBibleAdoptionV1.json is the machine-readable adoption/triage layer.
Data/GlobalWarehouseSourceRegistryV2.json is expanded from the Bible with high-value sources and corrected disabled/legacy routes.
Production waves cover world surfaces, vegetation/biomes, character/animation, VFX, audio, music, terrain/scanning and Arabic/UI across the whole game.
REFERENCE_ONLY/QUARANTINE/DISABLED sources do not auto-promote into distributable production.
DEC-037 still governs PRIVATE_OFFLINE_ONLY vs DISTRIBUTABLE_FRAMEWORK asset isolation.
DEC-038 still governs whole-game playable-film canon-safe design; resources serve the story rather than altering it.
performance_contract: 1K/2K default runtime textures; 4K only for measured hero assets.
Production textures use PNG/TGA, preferably channel-packed.
Heavy runtime assets use soft references + FStreamableManager async loading.
Crowds use pooling; repeated world detail uses ISM/HISM + LOD/culling.
High-poly scans/vegetation require decimation/retopo/LOD/material-slot and overdraw review before integration.

decisions.title: Immediate develop integration and dead-branch self-cleanup
decisions.resolution: develop is the canonical and continuously current integration branch. Every completed temporary branch must be exact-head validated, merged into develop immediately, then have its remote ref deleted automatically. develop must never be left behind completed work. The only temporary exceptions are an active PR head or a branch with verified unique unsalvaged commits; those branches remain protected only until selective salvage or explicit supersession is complete.
implementation_contract: Use one short-lived single-purpose branch/PR for a coherent engineering wave; batch related multi-file changes before publishing to avoid superseded runs.
After exact-head required validation succeeds, merge the completed branch into develop immediately; do not accumulate completed branches waiting for later consolidation.
Branch Cleanup runs automatically after every merged PR, targets the merge commit, and deletes the merged branch ref when it has no unique commits and is no longer an active PR head.
Branch Cleanup enumerates live remote refs once per run and auto-deletes every non-protected, non-active-PR zero-ahead branch; historical absent-ref lists are not recurring work.
Branches with ahead_by > 0 are retained only for selective salvage/supersession and must not become alternate trunks.
GitHub is the live authority for PR/branch/workflow transport state; the Governor stores durable policy, execution order and evidence boundaries only.
decisions.evidence_boundary: Branch/process governance only; no gameplay acceptance claim.

decisions.title: Smart-fence acceleration for the massive production build
